**Tokens**: The design tokens such as breakpoints and color manifests that underlie the visual system. - **Foundations**: The reference pages showing color, type, spacing, and radius primitives behind the components. - **Atoms**: The smallest reusable interface pieces like buttons, text, images, and icons. - **Molecules**: Small composed components like cards, fields, menus, and section headers built from atoms. - **Organisms**: Larger composed building blocks such as slides, decks, charts, and timelines used to assemble full pieces. - **Charts**: The chart building blocks such as legends, scales, and data tables used by data visualization organisms. - **Templates**: Full page templates, such as the talk template, that arrange components into a finished piece. - **Runtime**: The client and server runtime that renders components, hydrates islands, and serves pages. - **App Shell**: The top level app entry and setup files that wire the library together for preview and rendering. - **MCP Server**: A server that lets an AI agent query the 540 design system while it assembles a piece of content. - **MCP Tools**: The individual queries an agent can call, covering components, patterns, templates, tokens, rules, and images. - **MCP Transports**: The ways the server can be reached, over HTTP, stdio, or Firebase hosting. - **MCP Metadata**: The generated metadata and image catalog describing components, patterns, and tokens for the tools to read. - **Build and Check Scripts**: The command line scripts that build, render, and validate the design system and its pieces. - **Piece Rendering**: The scripts that render a finished piece from the template and check its structure, spelling, and rules. - **Runtime Panel**: A debugging overlay panel used while checking rendered pieces at runtime. --- predictable: spec --- # Piece rendering The piece renderer (scripts/render: index.mjs, core.mjs, parse.mjs, rules.mjs and spelling.mjs) turns a talk written with tags into one self-contained HTML page. renderTalk(source, {pieces, baseDir, lang, origin}) throws 'renderTalk needs the pieces folder' when pieces is not given; otherwise it reads pieces/manifest.json and returns {html, version, components, islands, scripts, warnings}, where version is the manifest's version, islands lists the island components the page hydrates and scripts says whether the page carries any script. The page has set to lang, else to the talk's own language, else 'es'; its head has and the talk's ; the component CSS is inlined in one <style> with every font of manifest.base.fonts embedded as a data:font/woff2;base64 URL, and every image is embedded as a base64 data URL. A talk made only of static components gives a page with no <script> and no <ds-island>; a talk with islands such as Deck, Steps and Statements gives a page that ships their scripts inline and wraps each island in <ds-island>; inside Steps, a Step's content that is itself a component or SVG is passed as encoded props ({$el, p}) and plain copy as a {$slot}. A talk may also be a page for the browser runtime, its tags inside one <script type="text/rev">: it renders to the same HTML as the plain tags, its data-lang gives the language unless lang is given, errors point to the line and column of the file, and the renderer throws a TagError when there is more than one such block ('only one <script type="text/rev"> per page') or content outside it ('the whole talk goes inside it'). A syntax problem is not collected: parse (parse.mjs) throws at the first one it meets (an unknown entity, a comment or a tag never closed, a malformed or repeated attribute, a closing tag that does not match the open one), and prepareTalk (core.mjs) throws it alone as a TagError '<origin> has 1 problem:'. Once the document parses, every problem prepareTalk finds is collected and thrown together as one TagError '<origin> has <n> problem(s):' with one line per problem: an unknown tag, with the nearest known tag as 'did you mean'; a value outside a prop's options ('<prop> is one of …, not "<value>"'); an attribute the component does not take; plain HTML other than the phrasing tags strong, em, b, i, code, small, sub, sup, br and a (with href); a field a JSON prop does not have; a component that cannot be used from a tag; a missing required prop; content in a component that takes none; a remote image ('points to a remote image') or an image file that does not exist ('image not found'); and, inside a Schema drawing (rev-schema and rev-schema-layer), a class outside the Schema vocabulary, an SVG attribute outside the allowed list such as fill, or a <rev-…> component.
